question.problem: A $500\,\text{L}$-capacity water tank initially holds $320\,\text{L}$ of water containing $20\,\text{kg}$ of a dissolved contaminant. Clean water begins to flow into the tank at a rate of $9\,\text{L/min},$ while the completely mixed water flows out at a rate of $5\,\text{L/min}.$ Find, rounded to two decimal places, the amount of contaminant in the tank at the moment it begins to overflow.
question.worked_solution:
Let $Q$ be the amount of contaminant in the tank at time $t.$ Then, the derivative

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

describes how this amount changes with respect to time $t,$ in minutes. This is equal to the rate at which contaminant enters the tank minus the rate at which contaminant leaves the tank.

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}
$$

Note that the units of $\frac{dQ}{dt},{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}$ and ${Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}$ are $\text{kg/min}.$ Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which contaminant enters the tank.

First, note that clean water (i.e., water containing $0\,\text{kg/L}$ of contaminant) enters the tank at a rate of $9\,\text{L/min}.$ So, the rate at which the *contaminant* enters the tank is

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′} & =(0\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}})\cdot (9\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =0\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which contaminant exits the tank.

To find the rate at which contaminant leaves the tank, we must first determine the volume of water in the tank at time $t.$

The tank initially contains $320\,\text{L}$ of water; clean water enters at $9\,\text{L/min},$ and mixed water leaves at $5\,\text{L/min}.$
As a result, the amount of water in the tank after $t$ minutes is

$$
V(t)=320+9t-5t=(320+4t)\,\text{L}.
$$

Note that $V(t)$ is an increasing function, so the tank is filling.

Since $Q$ is the amount of contaminant in the tank, the *concentration* of the water at time $t$ is

$$
\frac{Q}{320+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}}.
$$

Therefore, as the completely mixed water leaves at a rate of $5\,\text{L/min},$ *contaminant* leaves at a rate of

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} & =(5\,\frac{\text{L}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{320+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{L}}) \\  & =\frac{5Q}{320+4t}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}} \\  & =\frac{5Q}{4(80+t)}\,\frac{\text{kg}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.

The rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt} & ={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} \\  & =0-\frac{5Q}{4(80+t)},\end{aligned}
$$

which gives

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}=-\frac{5}{4(80+t)}\,Q.
$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.

Separating variables and integrating both sides with respect to $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{Q}\cdot \frac{dQ}{dt} & =-\frac{5}{4(80+t)} \\ \int \frac{1}{Q}\,dQ & =-\frac{5}{4}\int \frac{1}{80+t}\,dt \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡|Q| & =-\frac{5}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡|80+t|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus,

$$
Q(t)=\frac{A}{(80+t)^{5/4}}.
$$

Using the initial condition $Q(0)=20,$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{A}{{80}^{5/4}} & =20 \\ A & =20(80)^{5/4}.\end{aligned}
$$

So,

$$
Q(t)=20{(\frac{80}{80+t})}^{5/4}.
$$

Now, let ${t}_{o}$ be the time when the tank begins to overflow. Since the tank has a capacity of $500\,\text{L},$

$$
\begin{aligned}V({t}_{o}) & =500 \\ 320+4{t}_{o} & =500 \\ 4{t}_{o} & =180 \\ {t}_{o} & =45\,\text{min}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the amount of contaminant in the tank at the moment it begins to overflow is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(45)7 & =20{(\frac{80}{80+45})}^{5/4} \\  & =20{(\frac{80}{125})}^{5/4} \\  & ≈11.45\,\text{kg},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.
